edbDesc: An optical phenomenon in which linearly polarised light undergoes a small shift, parallel to the direction of propagation, when totally internally reflected. This effect is the linear polarisation analog of the Imbert-Fedorov effect. This occurs because the reflections of a finite sized beam will interfere along a line transverse to the average propagation direction.
title: Goos-Hänchen Effect
pickWhy: The sideways shift of totally reflected light is a fraction of a wavelength, far too small to do a job at a useful size.
